title: Claude or ChatGPT: which should you choose for a business in Romania?

body:
Claude or ChatGPT: which should you choose for a business in Romania? The right answer is not a single name, but a shortlist of the team's real tasks, set against two sets of pricing plans and features.

Below is a comparison by use case, with prices copied from the official pages on 27 August 2026. Check them again before buying, because providers change them often.

Claude or ChatGPT: which should you choose for a business in Romania?

Both tools start with a simple text chat, but quickly diverge depending on the plan: one has a dedicated coding assistant, direct Microsoft 365 integration and a team billing model with standard and premium seats; the other has its own coding assistant, a cheaper mid-tier plan and access to different models at each price level.

For a small business in Romania, the difference that matters most is the monthly budget per employee, not the name of the underlying model.

What the difference between the two actually means

Claude or ChatGPT should not be chosen based on a single test of answer quality, because both produce text, code and summaries of comparable quality for ordinary office tasks. The practical difference appears in three areas: which plan gives you access to the most capable model, which integrations it already has with tools you use and how much it costs for your actual number of employees.

Claude, made by Anthropic, comes with Claude Code for writing and debugging code directly from the terminal, Claude for Microsoft 365 and connectors through the MCP protocol, useful for businesses connecting several internal tools. ChatGPT, made by OpenAI, comes with Codex for code, projects and scheduled tasks, and custom GPTs for repetitive workflows.

Both have a functional free version for a quick test, but free usage limits are tight enough that they cannot support daily business work.

Prices and plans, checked on 27 August 2026

The prices below are copied from the two providers' official pricing pages at the time this article was written. They are not estimates and do not include VAT.

Claude plans

  • Free: 0 dollars per month, access to Claude in the browser and on your phone, with limited usage.
  • Pro: 17 dollars per month on an annual subscription (200 dollars paid upfront) or 20 dollars per month with monthly payment, with more usage and access to Claude Code.
  • Max: from 100 dollars per month, with 5 times or 20 times more usage than the Pro plan.
  • Team: standard seat 20 dollars per month with annual billing or 25 dollars with monthly billing; premium seat 100 dollars per month annually or 125 dollars monthly; available for teams of 2 to 150 people.

ChatGPT plans

  • Free: 0 dollars per month, unlimited text chat with the basic model, but with limits on images, voice and deep research.
  • Go: 8 dollars per month, more messages and uploads, may include ads.
  • Plus: 20 dollars per month, access to the advanced reasoning model and expanded Codex.
  • Pro: from 100 dollars per month, with 5 times or 20 times more usage, access to the most capable model and unlimited image generation.
  • Business: available from 2 users, price set through discussion with the sales team.

Note the symmetry: for a single user, both reach 20 dollars per month for the mid-tier plan and 100 dollars for the high-usage plan. The difference for a small business appears in the team plans, where Claude Team starts from 2 people with mixed standard and premium seats.

Content writing and customer communication

For blog articles, product descriptions or review replies, both tools maintain a requested tone well and follow a given structure if the prompt is clear and includes examples. The difference lies in memory and document organisation.

Claude organises conversations into projects with attached documents, useful for a brand guide kept consistent across sessions. ChatGPT does the same through projects and a memory that retains preferences between separate conversations, without needing to re-upload the documents every time.

For teams that often write customer replies with a review generator or carry out keyword research with Claude and ChatGPT, prompt quality matters more than the tool's name. A step-by-step guide to building a good prompt helps more than choosing between the two brands.

A simple test that works for both: give the tool three real examples of text that has already worked on your website and ask it to continue in the same tone, not a generic style. The tool that maintains the requested tone across ten consecutive replies, without drifting into filler, is the one worth paying for your content team.

Also check how each tool handles revisions. An assistant that accepts a short comment such as "shorter and no superlatives" and applies it across the whole text saves more time than a slightly better initial answer.

Code, automation and technical tasks for small businesses

Businesses that already have a server administrator or a part-time developer benefit from the coding agents in both ecosystems. Claude Code works directly from the terminal, reads an entire repository and can run commands with confirmation at every risky step. Codex, the OpenAI version, works similarly, integrated into ChatGPT and popular code editors.

For simple automations, such as generating a monthly report from a CSV export or filling in a repetitive template, the difference between the two is small. It matters more whether the team already has an account on one platform, because learning a new tool costs more time than the price difference between plans.

  • First check what the team does manually and repetitively each week.
  • Test both tools on their free plans, using the same real task, not an invented example.
  • Choose a paid plan only after seeing which responds faster to revisions.

Both coding agents can install packages, edit configuration files and run test commands, but ask for confirmation before irreversible actions such as deleting a file or publishing directly to the server. For a website on cPanel or Linux, this step-by-step confirmation matters more than the model's raw speed, because a mistake on a production server costs far more than the time saved.

Integration with tools the team already uses

For a business built around Microsoft 365, Claude has a direct integration, with Researcher and access to files in Outlook and SharePoint. For a business built around Google Workspace, Claude connects through dedicated connectors, while ChatGPT has its own extensions for Gmail and Drive.

If the business already has processes that use the Model Context Protocol, Claude includes remote MCP connectors in its paid plans, making it easier to connect internal tools built by you or a technical partner.

Do not choose a tool only for its current integration. Also check what changes if the business moves to a different software suite next year, because migrating conversations and projects between providers is not automatic.

For businesses managing several WordPress websites, both tools can generate maintenance scripts or explain an error message from the server log, but neither should insert code directly into a live website without human review first. The rule is the same as for any code received from a new colleague: read it first, run it afterwards.

Privacy of business and customer data

For team plans, both providers state that they do not use the content you enter to train new models by default. For individual plans, both offer an option to opt out of training, but it must be explicitly enabled in the account settings.

Before entering customer data, contracts or internal prices into a conversation, read the current privacy policy for the chosen plan, not an assumption from memory. Policies change, and a business working with personal data needs written confirmation, not an impression.

  • Do not enter customers' medical or financial data without a data processing agreement with the provider.
  • Explicitly enable the training opt-out option if you use an individual plan.
  • Prefer the team plan for any document containing real customer data.

For a broader check of how your website handles visitor data, an E-E-A-T audit shows where trust signals are missing, regardless of the AI tool used internally.

How to choose in practice

If the business writes mostly marketing content and rarely code, Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus do the same job at the same price, and the decision comes down to which interface feels more natural to the team. If the business has a developer working in the terminal daily, Claude Code is worth testing first, because it was built for that workflow.

If the team already has a paid Microsoft 365 subscription, Claude's integration shortens the time to the first useful result. If the team depends on Google Workspace and extensions already installed for Gmail, ChatGPT has a similar advantage there.

The safest test remains a direct one: take a task you repeat each week, run it on both tools' free plans and compare the time it takes to get a result that no longer needs much correction.

Conclusion

There is no single answer to Claude or ChatGPT, but a different answer for each business, depending on budget, existing integrations and daily tasks.
